penicillamine, a chelating agent that binds copper, was administered to male golden hamster to study the effects of penicillamine on connective tissues after bleomycin-induced lung injury.

penicillamine administration to hamsters after a single dose of bleomycine increased lung compliance and total lung capacity, decreased lung elastance and resistance, and increased the proportion of soluble collagen and glycosaminoglysacns, but not total collagen or elastin, when compared to animals that received bleomycine alone.
(1) penicillamine increases soluble collagen in the lungs, (2) penicillamide decreases glycosaminoglycerans in the lungs, and (3) penicillaminde has no effect on elastin in the lungs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of penicillamine on the connective tissue components and lung statics of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in hamsters.
the effects of bleomycin on lung connective tissues, lung statics, and the effect of penicillamine on these parameters.
the role of collagen and glycosaminoglucans in the pathogenesis of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in hamsters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of penicillamine on the lung are not as great as the effects of bleomycin on the lung, and penicillamine has a limited role in the prevention or treatment of bleomycin-induced fibrosis in hamsters.
penicillamine, when administered after a bleomycin-induced fibrosis, does alter connective tissue expression in the lungs of hamsters.
penicillamine does not alter the mechanical properties of the bleomcyin-injured lung.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
penicillamine does not reverse the bleomycin-induced lung injury in the hamster.
penicillamine is not a useful treatment for pulmonary fibrosis in the hamster model.
, in this model of lung fibrosis, penicillamine does not improve lung function, but may be beneficial by preventing further connective tissue changes in the lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
penicillamine does not improve the mechanical properties of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
the mechanical behavior of the lung is not simply a function of the connective tissue levels.
penicillamine is not a good treatment for bleomycin-induced lung injury.
